summary: This benchmark paper investigates activation transplantation failure between language models by evaluating an affine input map connecting Qwen2.5-14B to the final feed-forward block of Qwen2.5-Coder-7B. Using a controlled 256-group minimal-pair bracket completion evaluation, the authors demonstrate that the affine mapping attenuates and reverses the native bracket completion log-odds signal (from +2.043 to -0.242). The methodology is tightly controlled and highly reproducible, though limited in empirical scope to a single model pair and task.
strengths: Rigorous causal intervention design isolating the feed-forward module input state while holding residual and readout states constant.
Exceptional reproducibility documentation, citing exact model revisions, CPython commit hashes, ridge penalty formulations, and specific software versions.
Sound statistical methodology utilizing paired bootstrap confidence intervals and balanced minimal prompt pairs across bracket types.
Honest discussion of scope limitations, explicitly acknowledging that findings are restricted to one affine calibration on one model pair.
weaknesses: Narrow benchmark scope confined to bracket closure logits rather than broader multi-token coding capabilities or semantic tasks.
Evaluates only a single linear/affine translation architecture without comparing against non-linear probes, Procrustes alignment, or low-rank adapters.
Lacks verification across multiple intermediate layer pairings between the host and donor models.
suggestions: Compare the simple ridge regression affine map against orthogonal Procrustes alignment or a small non-linear MLP adapter to evaluate whether representational distortion is inherently linear.
Broaden the evaluation panel to other structured syntax benchmarks beyond bracket closure, such as indentation or keyword pairing.
Formally supply the GitHub repository link in the submission metadata rather than solely as inline markdown references.

claims.text: The donor has 28 blocks of width 3,584 and the host has 48 blocks of width 5,120.
The frozen donor was Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B... The frozen host was Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B
The fit solves (X.T @ X + lambda * I) W = X.T @ Y, with lambda equal to 0.02 times the mean diagonal entry of X.T @ X.
